english: He brings these things to bear against those whom he was writing to: 'when your obedience is fulfilled, look to the outward appearance.' There is a difference in understanding this word: if it were expressed commandingly, it would mean this: if, O Corinthians, your obedience is fulfilled through agreement with the divine teaching, observe the outward appearance; for in this way you will know those who present themselves as sheep but are inwardly ravening wolves, and the truly genuine teachers, to whom it was said, 'You are the light of the world' (Matt 5:14). In this way, having observed, the impostors whom you also cast out will be known to you, as will the true apostles of Christ, in whom you also desired to believe willingly. This agrees with 'by their fruits you will know them' (Matt 7:16).

But if it were expressed definitively, 'look to the outward appearance,' it suggests such a thought: judge the disposition of the teachers and the disciples by the power, always gazing intently at the outward aspect of those speaking, being deceived by those attending only to the outward appearance alone. If anyone, then, being a wolf, pretends to be a sheep, merely bringing a fleece, receive this one as a false apostle, but the one being a prophet, receive him as an apostle and prophet. For certainly some, pretending to be disciples of Christ, but being truly acquainted with the one transforming into an angel of light, caused deception among some of you, as if there were no resurrection of the dead nor the rational soul intervening after the separation from the body. Therefore, having doubt as to how 'look to the outward appearance' is expressed, the former understanding holds as the teaching.

Regarding 2 Cor 10:17-18: Having sufficiently refuted those teaching the opposite as if they were merely making a noise as Christ's, he necessarily brought forward that one must boast in the Lord, he who unblemishedly and sincerely relies on glory; for not he who proves himself to be approved is of such a kind in every way, but he whom the Lord has established through testimony. Having shown how it is the folly of the foolish to praise themselves, and that the Corinthians are rather led astray by such people, he says to them: 'I wish you would endure me speaking about myself what they also say about themselves; for having many true things to write, I requested not to, knowing that it seems foolish to talk about oneself. english: Regarding the heavenly ones, thus someone being surrounded [by the body] is still able to be guided by the vision of the mind in heaven and the paradise to become [such].

Another will say that whether in a body or outside of a body, he writes not about his own body in which the soul is surrounded, but about the whole [state], so that the thing said might be such: snatched up even to the third heaven and into the paradise (2 Cor 12:4). Whether these things are a body or incorporeal, I do not know; for the knowledge of these things rests with the Father of Wisdom, God.

And the 'even to the third heaven' also contains ambiguity; for from the ambiguity it is signified whether, it being the case of the greater number of heavens, he reached up to the third to understand the things there—and let this be numbered from the firmament; for this is the first heaven for those being taken up entirely—or whether, it being the case of one heaven, he reached up to the third part of it. However it may be, God would know and whom He would himself make manifest; nevertheless, two snatchings are made evident: even to the third heaven and even into the paradise.

But it must be said regarding the things said, that he did not say anything about the third heaven as one who has heard or seen something; for concerning the one who announced how he heard in it unutterable words (2 Cor 12:4), which it is not possible for man to speak—unless indeed one takes commonly 'I heard unutterable words even in the third heaven or heaven and into the paradise.' However it may be, it is made evident that the paradise is a school of divine lessons.

And what does he intend by the unutterable words? Let it be known how much the one speaking them uses not syllables and sounds, being unutterable, compared to how much they have the truth, having the essence in divine intellect; and these things are heard not by the reception of sense but by the contemplation of divine intellect. For the God-Word Himself being Christ, does not neglect, speaking not to Paul but in Paul; and thus He also taught, becoming toward each of the prophets. If therefore the Savior speaks in the saints, the things said are unutterable; for if they were spoken words, He would have struck their hearing, and not...

He spoke in them, but to them. And it is even the case that it is not within a man's power to speak. For indeed it is possible for a man to hear, having an enlightened understanding, but it is impossible to speak those things with voices and syllables; for these are the speaking elements. 'Not within power' is said instead of 'possible'. This is not said only here, but also in other letters of the one writing these things; for everything is permitted, but not everything is profitable, which is equal to being able to do all things.

Having said this, he necessarily brought forward the divine revelations and visions: 'I will boast about a man such as this being in Christ, but about myself I speak boldly only concerning the aforementioned weaknesses' (2 Cor 12:7-9). And he who says these things is not another from the one who has seen the visions; except if he is indeed the same, he differs in thought—how indeed he is understood as a weak man because of the intention of the condescension, but how he is understood as having ascended super-eminently and being in Christ because of the vision.

Others, not wishing to give an occasion, and [claiming] that no way is strong enough to let the evil one inflict any diseases, and not enduring that perfect men should undergo much regarding the health of the body—for they will say they have learned to endure those who oppress them—will say: 'Someone having received many and great visions, if he were not overcome by human weakness, would think greatly of himself.' In order that he might not have room, the power guarding the ruling principle of God often manages for the one being guarded to be outside the protection of it, so that they might slip in and take a human thought.

And since perfect men shut out even the contamination in the intellect, they think they have a great disaster, even if a memory is cast upon them by a satanic angel. Therefore, they indeed entreat to be cleansed also from secret things and to not have any awareness of something trivial. And that this is so, he knew, being afflicted, to flee to God, as he shows having written: 'Concerning this distressing satanic angel, three times I entreated the Lord, so that he might be removed from me. And the Lord said to me, whom I entreated: My grace is sufficient for you; for you shall know through...'

english: Completion does not exist by its own power, but by our cooperation. Regarding the three times, one might say that the three makes things manifest; for from the three comes abundance, for the three are many.

Do not think that we are defending ourselves to you (2 Cor 12:19); for we have not previously been set to please men, but God (2 Cor 12:20). We intend good things before God and also before men, so that we may be revealed to God, persuading men rightly by life and fitting speech; for speaking in Christ, we are additionally speaking for God, as seeing His purpose, we do all things and say all things. Therefore, I am confident that having read this letter sincerely, you will depart from whispering, having rejected it as slave-like; for the boldness of slaves is in muttering and grumbling. But also turn away from contentions and the quarrels arising from them and from ambition; for thus it will follow that you find what you desire.

For a teacher who is prosperous in listeners, in whom he can speak wisdom, is tossed about and greatly puffed up, but is immediately humbled when those approaching need reproof and conviction regarding what they are doing badly. For if they practice fornication and uncleanness and the following debauchery and do not repent, they have died the death of the soul; so that one having a nurturing disposition toward them should rather mourn them than those building empty tombs for those who have departed from philosophy. For sensation loves to be near to those sinning, when others mourn for them with wailing. The Savior is able even according to this to bless those who mourn, since after the evil from mourning they shall be comforted by God. But because he says 'lest coming again I be humbled' (2 Cor 13:1), he shows that even previously he has sufficiently experienced this toward them, having turned them toward repentance. Therefore, he brought it about by necessity; behold, this third time I come to you, so that having the third visit instead of three witnesses, [we may be] certain.

They are established. For if by the mouth of two or three witnesses every word is brought forth according to a judgment, it is established and confirmed; thus it was necessary through the two appearances [of which] I have made you certain. And since you need the fullness of being confirmed, I decided to answer you a third time. 2 Cor 13:10: I had authority over you to build you up as a city and a temple of God; and this authority I want to bear fruit, through which I write teaching that I have authority not for destruction, but for building up.

44 2 Cor 13:11: After all exhortation, he advises, having taken up oneness of mind, to hasten toward a good end; possessing [themselves], they will receive genuine virtue and faith. For thus they have support, thinking the same thing, bringing peace, so that the space of the love of God might come to be among them. For this presence will make it an immovable possession for them, as each one imitating the teacher, to say: who will separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus? And the following. 2 Cor 13:12-13: By power he says this; thus all the saints know you, just as they greet you, from where knowing such great men, you practice and think what they accept. The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ and the love of God and the communion of the Holy Spirit with all of you; Amen.

It shall be, he says, for those thus blessed, the grace of the Lord Jesus, that is, saving them without works or making them having been graced. And the love of God shall be with them according to which he loves them or they [love] him with all heart and soul, and the communion of the Holy Spirit approaches, making spiritual and holy those who partake of it. We also do all things and say, as the blessed John says, so that they may also appear worthy of the love of God and attain the things that are coming by the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom belongs the glory and the dominion for the ages of ages; Amen.
